links.outcome: Stigmatizing associations in LLM outputs when a Black-associated SAE latent is activated
links.effect: The Black latent activates on terms like "incarceration", and activating it increases the risk assigned to a patient becoming "belligerent".
links.quote: For example, activating the Black latent increases the risk assigned to the probability that a patient will become "belligerent".

links.outcome: Effectiveness of SAE latent steering for mitigating racial bias in LLM outputs
links.effect: Steering improved bias in simple settings but was less successful for realistic, complex clinical tasks; described as of marginal utility for realistic tasks.
links.quote: We find that this offers improvements in simple settings, but is less successful for more realistic and complex clinical tasks.

links.effect: SAEs identified Gemma-2 latents correlated with Black individuals; the latent activated on “African American” and “incarceration”.
links.quote: We find that this latent activates on reasonable input sequences (e.g., "African American") but also problematic words like "incarceration".

links.effect: Steering toward the Black latent induced problematic associations in outputs about Black patients.
links.quote: We then show that we can use this latent to steer models to generate outputs about Black patients, and further that this can induce problematic associations in model outputs as a result.
